title: Sheng Tseng-Yien, Chinese Student Deported From Japan On Suspicion Of Being Connected With Communists

page_data.en:

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ...
S.I, Special Branch. No. 7772
REPORT
Date February 4, 1937.
Sheng Tseng-yien (盛忠亮), Chinese student deported from Japan
on suspicion of being connected with communists.
D.I. Kuh Pao Hwa Forwarded by
With reference to the attached report on the subject of
Sheng Tseng Yien, Chinese student deported from Japan, who
was suspected of being connected with the activities of members
of the Communist Party, I have to state that this individual
arrived in Shanghai on January 25. 1937, on board the s.s.
"Tsukuba Maru". Following this, he proceeded to the China
Hotel, No.160 Kweichow Road, where he stayed until the morning
of January 27. During his sojourn in the hotel, he had no
visitors and seldom went out. It is said that he has since
returned to his native place in Chekiang Province.
Particulars of the aforementioned suspect have been
recorded by this office for future reference.
Kuh Pao. hwa
D. I.
D.C. (Special Branch).
Jiu

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. REG.
S. D. 772
S. 1. Special Branch Station, 2 37
REPORT
Date February 2, 1937.
Subject Information regarding a Chinese Student named Sheng Tseng Yien.
Made by J. S. Kamashita Forwarded by I. Boyne D.S.I.

The following report dated January 20, 1937, regarding
a Chinese student named Sheng Tseng Yien has been received by
the local Japanese Consular Police from the Tokyo Police:-
Sheng Tseng Yien(盛澄淵), aged 23, native of Siao
Hsien(蕭縣), Chekiang Province, graduated from the Chekiang
University Agricultural School, Hanchow, in June 1934, and
arrived in Tokyo in October of the same year for the purpose
of studying Japanese language. Between February and March,
1935, he was taught Japanese by Hamako Watanabe, a communist
suspect, residing at No. 59 Komagome Sadagicho, Hongo Ward.
He also attended the Toha School in Kanda Ward. In March,
1936, he was admitted to the Special Class of the First High
School, Tokyo.
He is suspected of being connected with communists prior
to his arrival in Japan. On several occasions he interviewed
Sakuro Watanabe, a relative of Hamako Watanabe, who is now
attempting to reestablish the "Zenkyo", a communist labour union.
Sheng has given the sum of Yen 170 to Hamako Watanabe
for living expenses. He also intended to supply funds to
further the activities of Sakuro Watanabe.
As it is considered that the Sheng's residence in Japan
was detrimental to peace and order he was instructed to leave
the country. He left for Shanghai by the s.s. "Tsukuba
Maru" which sailed from Yokohama on January 19, 1937.

S.I.
(D. I. Kuh)
Inquiry recd.
J. Kamashita
D.
